statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk is low and well below the block threshold, while Stress stays moderate because a record Nasdaq-100 close sits alongside Treasury yields near 19-year highs.
recommendation: Conditions remain consistent with normal mean-reverting behaviour. A narrow caution window is published for 13:30-14:30Z, covering the US cash open, the flash PMI and the start of the Fed Barr remarks, where two-sided repricing is most likely.
headline: NQ futures ease to 31,011 after retracing from the overnight high; low Tail and moderate Stress into the 13:45Z flash PMI
body: Nasdaq-100 futures are near 31,011, down about 0.06%, after retracing roughly 84 points from the 31,094.75 overnight high inside a two-sided range of about 112 points. That retracement matters more than the level: the pathological no-retracement path that defines Tail risk is not present, and VIX at 14.14 shows no overnight volatility expansion. The backdrop is a record Nasdaq-100 cash close at 30,732.40, up 0.82%, with the session high of 30,770.63 marking the index's first record since June. Leadership was narrow rather than broad. Memory and storage names led, with the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index up about 2% for a sixth straight gain, while megacaps were split roughly evenly and the Dow fell 185 points. Narrow leadership concentrates single-story risk but argues against an index-wide one-way trend. The offsetting factor is cross-asset conflict rather than directional efficiency. The 10-year Treasury yield near 4.96% and the 2-year near 4.76% remain close to 19-year highs, which keeps long-duration valuations sensitive, yet yields were steady overnight rather than repricing. Brent near $99.3 has eased through five losing sessions on reporting that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days if US military pressure and the port blockade are lifted. That report is publicly disputed by Iranian state-linked media, so the oil channel is a genuine two-sided headline risk rather than a directional input. The near-term checkpoint stack is the 13:30Z US cash open, the 13:45Z S&P Global flash PMI with composite consensus around 55.2 after 56.0 in August, Fed Vice Chair Barr at 14:05Z, EIA crude inventories at 14:30Z and the 5-year note auction at 17:00Z. These are catalysts, not automatic blocks. Before they print, hypothetical post-event alignment is not treated as observed, so they raise Stress and shape the published forecast path while Tail stays low on current evidence.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding clock hours carry a published Claude assessment. Tail ran 10-21, with three WATCH hours around the 22 September US cash session and power hour, then decayed through the Asian and European overnight to 10-12 as the post-record path stayed orderly. Stress eased from the mid-40s to the low 30s before ticking back to 36, and dominant mode rotated from trend-up through mixed back to normal. No hour in the window reached the block threshold.
outlookSummary: The published path holds Tail low through the European morning, lifts it to a WATCH band of 20-21 for the two hours containing the 13:30Z US cash open, the 13:45Z flash PMI and the Barr remarks, then decays through the afternoon with a smaller bump around the 17:00Z 5-year auction and the 19:00-20:00Z power hour. Overnight into 24 September returns to 11-12 with confidence declining on forecast distance rather than on weaker evidence, and the final hours lift Stress modestly ahead of the 24 September jobless claims and Fed speaker stack. Every hour beyond the current one is conditional; no future price structure is treated as observed.
